summary.one_liner: The Hacker News is a cybersecurity news site; the captured page is a news item on Google letting approved third-party Android app stores do one-tap installs and background updates outside the US.
takeaways: Google's Registered App Stores program lets approved third-party Android stores request one-tap installs without the usual confirmation screens.
Approved stores can update apps in the background under the user's own update settings, starting December 1 on Android 17 QPR2 or later.
To qualify, a store must pass identity checks and send Google its full catalog plus every new app and update for ongoing malware scanning.
The feature is limited to supported countries, which do not include the US, and joining the program is optional.
Google announced the program in March alongside changes it said resolved its disputes with Epic Games.
summary.summary: This is a cybersecurity news front page, and the captured text is a single news story from October 28, 2026. It reports that Google will let approved third-party Android app stores install apps with one tap and update them in the background, without Android's usual confirmation screens. Stores must pass identity checks and submit their full catalog and all new apps and updates for malware scanning. The features apply from December 1 only on Android 17 QPR2 or later in supported countries, excluding the US.
